segments.name: Frontier AI Labs
segments.subtitle: Anthropic, xAI, other model-training labs at the frontier

compute_mfu.text: industry range ~35-50% for large transformer training; varies by parallelism strategy, fabric, and software stack

provenance.source: industry MFU range published in academic and infra papers (Megatron-LM, PaLM, Llama training reports, 2022-2024); operational targets, not a single benchmark
provenance.notes: MFU is workload-and-parallelism dependent — no single point value applies across labs; range is the honest representation

compute_time_to_train.text: wall-clock time depends on model size, parallelism strategy, fabric, and software stack; no universal comparable benchmark across frontier labs

provenance.source: TTT is reported in scattered ways across frontier labs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT-4, xAI Grok) and not as a directly comparable figure
provenance.notes: directional — TTT comparisons require apples-to-apples model + parallelism + token-count specifications that frontier labs typically do not publish

compute_checkpoint_resume_latency.text: fabric-bound at frontier scale; checkpoint write + resume cycles dominate cluster downtime windows when training models past the trillion-parameter mark

provenance.source: checkpoint-resume characterization for frontier-scale training — depends on fabric bisection bandwidth, parallel-write strategy, and storage tier; SHARP / NCCL collective ops are the structural lever
provenance.notes: directional — exact figures are workload-specific; cluster-design and storage-tier choices dominate

fabric_interconnect_throughput.text: effective bisection bandwidth across the cluster, not per-port; frontier scale (multi-thousand-GPU) requires aggregate fabric coordination

provenance.source: effective bisection bandwidth at frontier scale depends on topology (fat-tree, dragonfly, rail-optimized) and collective-op performance; per-port line rate is necessary but not sufficient
provenance.notes: directional — frontier labs evaluate aggregate fabric performance under collective-op load, not nameplate per-port throughput

compute_inference_p99.text: TTFT P95/P99 target ~300-500ms for interactive enterprise workloads (use-case dependent: chatbot ~500ms, code-completion ~100ms, batch/report tolerant to seconds)

provenance.source: industry LLM inference SLO conventions, 2026 (Spheron, Rafay, BentoML, Mirantis) — frontier labs typically self-host inference and inherit similar SLO targets for their API endpoints
provenance.notes: SLA convention/range — frontier inference at scale optimizes for cost-per-token vs latency; SLO inherited from the enterprise consumer context

ops_tco_capex_directional.text: factors: GPU count at multi-thousand-cluster scale, NVL72 rack-scale buildouts, fabric (Spectrum-X / Quantum-X800), facility power+cooling at multi-MW scale

provenance.source: deployment-class characterization for frontier-scale training clusters; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with OpEx. High band reflects multi-billion-dollar frontier-cluster buildouts (xAI Colossus, Anthropic compute commitments, Meta Llama training stack).

ops_tco_opex_directional.text: factors: continuous multi-MW power draw, MLops + research-engineering headcount, fabric tuning overhead, downtime cost (a single failed run can lose weeks of compute)

provenance.source: deployment-class characterization for frontier-scale operations; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with CapEx. High band reflects continuous power draw plus research-engineering headcount; frontier OpEx is structurally dominated by power and elite-talent costs.

ops_lead_time.text: frontier labs pre-commit capacity contracts with NVIDIA and cloud partners; effective lead-time is allocation-priority, not standard order-to-rack procurement

provenance.source: lead-time characterization for frontier labs — capacity is typically pre-purchased on multi-quarter or multi-year contracts; allocation queues are the binding constraint
provenance.notes: directional — frontier procurement is capacity-allocation-based, not order-to-rack; standard lead-time metrics do not apply

ops_service_footprint.text: direct vendor engineering partnership; frontier labs work with NVIDIA's top systems-engineering team, not regional sales

provenance.source: service-footprint characterization for frontier labs — direct engineering partnership model bypasses standard service channels
provenance.notes: directional — frontier labs receive concierge-level support; standard service-footprint metrics don't apply

ops_skills_fit.text: deep CUDA / collective-comm / parallelism expertise required; frontier labs hire ahead of the curve and contribute back to NVIDIA's stack (NCCL, Megatron, FlashAttention)

provenance.source: skills-fit characterization for frontier labs — engineering teams at Anthropic / OpenAI / xAI / Meta have NVIDIA-stack expertise that often exceeds NVIDIA's own application teams
provenance.notes: directional — frontier labs are talent-saturated on NVIDIA stack; skills-fit is high but for a narrow elite-engineer cohort, not broadly transferable

architecture_blend.note: Heavy NVL72 — trillion-parameter training requires unified 72-GPU NVLink domain

segments.isv_rationale: Scale-out parallel file system for trillion-parameter training; orchestration ISVs stripped away in favor of bare-metal/custom schedulers
segments.partner_intensity_rationale: buys frontier NVL72 relatively directly, but still needs OEM integration + service at scale

provenance.notes: Segment definition synthesized from public observations of frontier-lab infrastructure preferences (NVL72, very large scale).

segments.name: Hyperscalers
segments.subtitle: Azure, GCP, AWS hyperscale cloud operators

compute_tco_per_token.text: highly workload-dependent; industry estimates vary by an order of magnitude depending on model size, batch utilization, quantization strategy, and hardware amortization period

provenance.source: no universal benchmark — TCO-per-token varies dramatically by workload mix and MFU realization; published external estimates (SemiAnalysis, A16z, Together AI) span roughly an order of magnitude; hyperscaler-internal figures are confidential
provenance.notes: no universal benchmark — TCO-per-token is workload-defined; do NOT present as a cited point value

ops_pue.text: hyperscale PUE typically in the ~1.10-1.20 range (Google publishes the lowest, AWS / Azure publish in the same band); design ceiling near 1.0 with adiabatic cooling

provenance.source: public PUE disclosures — Google annual sustainability reports, AWS sustainability dashboard, Microsoft Azure sustainability calculator. Auditor-verified for sustainability reporting.
provenance.notes: PUE is one of the few hyperscaler operational metrics with reliable public citation; vendor numbers are externally verified

ops_fleet_availability.text: fleet availability targets typically 99.9-99.95% at hyperscale; failure budgets baked into the SLA tier sold to customers (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure OpenAI)

provenance.source: fleet availability characterized by hyperscaler SLA disclosures and incident post-mortems; realized availability varies by region and service tier
provenance.notes: directional — published SLA targets are the floor; realized availability often exceeds but is workload-and-region dependent

compute_hardware_density.text: rack density bound by power-and-cooling envelope; hyperscalers typically operate at 30-50 kW/rack with custom power distribution, vs ~15 kW for typical enterprise

provenance.source: hardware-density characterization for hyperscaler racks — Open Compute Project (OCP) reference designs, hyperscaler datacenter disclosures, Uptime Institute analyses
provenance.notes: directional — exact figures are facility-and-region specific; the 30-50 kW band is widely reported in OCP / industry analyses

compute_inference_p99.text: TTFT P95/P99 target ~300-500ms for interactive enterprise workloads (use-case dependent: chatbot ~500ms, code-completion ~100ms, batch/report tolerant to seconds)

provenance.source: industry LLM inference SLO conventions, 2026 (Spheron, Rafay, BentoML, Mirantis) — hyperscalers expose this as the SLA target on their inference APIs (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure OpenAI)
provenance.notes: SLA convention/range — hyperscalers publish SLO targets on their inference services; this is the customer-facing ceiling

ops_tco_capex_directional.text: factors: GPU count at multi-hundred-thousand cluster scale, custom-designed racks, fabric (NVIDIA stack and/or custom silicon — Trainium, TPU, Maia), facility buildouts at GW scale

provenance.source: deployment-class characterization for hyperscaler buildouts; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with OpEx. High band reflects multi-billion-dollar GPU procurement at hyperscale; volume discounts apply but absolute CapEx remains dominant.

ops_tco_opex_directional.text: factors: power-cost arbitrage (renewable PPAs), low PUE, automated MLops at scale, internal-customer monetization offsetting per-GPU OpEx

provenance.source: deployment-class characterization for hyperscaler operations; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with CapEx. Medium band (vs sovereign high / verticals high) reflects hyperscaler operational efficiency: renewable PPAs, automated MLops, and revenue offset from re-selling the same capacity to customers.

ops_lead_time.text: hyperscalers operate on multi-quarter committed-volume contracts with NVIDIA; effective lead-time is allocation-priority, not order-to-rack

provenance.source: lead-time characterization for hyperscalers — committed-volume agreements with NVIDIA shape allocation priority; standard lead-time metrics do not apply
provenance.notes: directional — hyperscalers compete for allocation, not for delivery slots; the binding constraint is NVIDIA capacity allocation

ops_service_footprint.text: global vendor partnership; hyperscalers maintain dedicated NVIDIA engineering relationships at the systems-engineering and roadmap level

provenance.source: service-footprint characterization for hyperscalers — global presence plus dedicated roadmap-level engineering partnership
provenance.notes: directional — hyperscalers operate as strategic partners, not standard customers; service-footprint metrics are not the relevant lens

ops_skills_fit.text: deep in-house CUDA / NVAIE expertise; hyperscalers maintain large platform-engineering teams optimized for the NVIDIA stack and increasingly contribute upstream

provenance.source: skills-fit characterization for hyperscalers — internal teams have multi-year operational experience with NVIDIA at scale; some hyperscalers contribute upstream to CUDA / NCCL / Triton
provenance.notes: directional — hyperscaler skills-fit is structurally high but increasingly bifurcated as some pursue custom silicon (Trainium, TPU, Maia)

architecture_blend.note: Blended NVL72 + HGX — direct co-engineering; OEM presence minimal

segments.partner_intensity_rationale: co-engineers directly with NVIDIA, OEM presence minimal (per matrix); largely self-integrates

provenance.notes: Segment definition synthesized from hyperscaler public infrastructure disclosures and analyst coverage.

segments.name: Fortune 500 Enterprise
segments.subtitle: Production AI workloads in regulated enterprises (e.g., JPMorgan-class)

compute_production_roi.text: positive but deployment-specific; driven by automation value vs infra+ops cost

provenance.source: no universal benchmark — ROI is deployment-specific and varies by use-case automation value, regulatory regime, and existing ops maturity
provenance.notes: no universal benchmark — ROI is deployment-specific; do NOT present as a cited figure

compute_inference_p99.text: TTFT P95/P99 target ~300-500ms for interactive enterprise workloads (use-case dependent: chatbot ~500ms, code-completion ~100ms, batch/report tolerant to seconds)

provenance.source: industry LLM inference SLO conventions, 2026 (Spheron, Rafay, BentoML, Mirantis published targets for interactive enterprise inference)
provenance.notes: SLA convention/range, not a single benchmark — keep the use-case-dependent caveat in the value

ops_deployment_cycle_time.text: weeks-to-months, depends on org MLops maturity and ISV fit

provenance.source: deployment-cycle bands characterized by enterprise MLops surveys; no single canonical number
provenance.notes: directional band — depends on org MLops maturity and ISV platform fit

ops_compliance_audit_time.text: depends on regulation + existing controls; ISV/software certification path is the main lever

provenance.source: compliance-cycle characterization varies by regulatory regime (SOC2 / HIPAA / FedRAMP / EU AI Act) and the maturity of the customer's control inventory
provenance.notes: directional — regulation-dependent and control-state-dependent

ops_tco_capex_directional.text: factors: GPU count, system (HGX baseboard + chassis), networking, facility readiness

provenance.source: deployment-class analyst characterization for HGX-class Fortune-500 deployments; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with OpEx by this module. High band reflects the iron-spend concentration of HGX-class buildouts (8x Blackwell baseboards + Spectrum-X networking + facility prep).

ops_tco_opex_directional.text: factors: power / PUE, MFU-realized utilization, MLops headcount, re-certification, downtime — moderated by NVAIE ecosystem maturity

provenance.source: deployment-class analyst characterization for HGX-class Fortune-500 operations; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with CapEx by this module. Medium band (vs CapEx high) reflects the moat thesis: NVAIE ecosystem maturity moderates OpEx — TensorRT-LLM / NIM / Dynamo are battle-tested vs alternative stacks, reducing MLops headcount and re-cert overhead.

architecture_blend.note: The classic blended portfolio: HGX for training, RTX PRO for inference

segments.isv_rationale: New servers in the data center — apply existing corporate policy/IAM/compliance; cloud-native favors OpenShift, infra-first favors VMware/Nutanix
segments.battleground_note: critical battleground for the Partner-PM — flawless execution across Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Cisco, Supermicro.
segments.partner_intensity_rationale: channel-served — Dell/HPE/Lenovo/Cisco/Supermicro integrate, certify, support; the partner ecosystem wins or loses the deal

provenance.notes: Segment definition synthesized from Fortune 500 enterprise AI deployment patterns (private cloud, regulated, audit-driven).

segments.name: Sovereign AI
segments.subtitle: Nation-state and regional AI programs (G42 UAE, EU sovereign, etc.)

ops_data_residency_pct.text: target 100% in-jurisdiction execution; depends on deployment topology and air-gap posture

provenance.source: no universal benchmark — data residency is a compliance posture, not a measured number; depends on national data-sovereignty law + deployment topology + air-gap discipline
provenance.notes: no universal benchmark — compliance posture, not a measured percentage; do NOT present as a cited figure

ops_air_gap_capability.text: full offline operation including updates and monitoring; depends on architecture

provenance.source: air-gap capability characterized by deployment topology; ISV platform support for offline update channels and isolated monitoring is the structural lever
provenance.notes: directional — architecture-dependent; ISV platform choice (OpenShift AI / VMware Private AI / Nutanix) sets the offline-operation ceiling

ops_portability_index.text: effort to migrate models / data across national clouds without lock-in; ISV platform choice is the main lever

provenance.source: portability characterized by ISV abstraction layer — Kubernetes / OCI containerization and open model formats are the structural enablers across sovereign jurisdictions
provenance.notes: directional — ISV platform choice is the structural lever; CUDA/NVAIE lock-in shifts the portability ceiling

ops_compliance_audit_time.text: regulation-dependent (national data-sovereignty law + sectoral); control-inventory maturity dependent

provenance.source: compliance-cycle characterization varies by national regime (UAE PDPL, EU AI Act + GDPR, regional data-sovereignty laws) and sectoral overlay; control-inventory maturity is the dominant variable
provenance.notes: directional — regulation-regime-dependent and control-state-dependent

ops_security_perimeter.text: unauthorized-access attempt frequency at infrastructure level; directional posture, not a measured rate

provenance.source: perimeter posture characterized by defense-in-depth architecture — physical, network, identity, and crypto layers; metrics surface at audit cadence, not as live counters
provenance.notes: directional — posture is architecture-bound; numerical attempt-rate metrics are organization-specific and not publicly comparable

compute_inference_p99.text: TTFT P95/P99 target ~300-500ms for interactive enterprise workloads (use-case dependent: chatbot ~500ms, code-completion ~100ms, batch/report tolerant to seconds)

provenance.source: industry LLM inference SLO conventions, 2026 (Spheron, Rafay, BentoML, Mirantis published targets for interactive enterprise inference) — applies to sovereign deployments serving interactive workloads within their jurisdiction
provenance.notes: SLA convention/range, not a single benchmark — keep the use-case-dependent caveat; sovereign deployments inherit the same SLO ceiling for interactive workloads

ops_tco_capex_directional.text: factors: GPU count, system (HGX baseboard + chassis), networking, facility readiness, in-jurisdiction siting, sovereign procurement overhead

provenance.source: deployment-class analyst characterization for sovereign AI buildouts; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with OpEx. High band reflects sovereign-program scale (frontier-class deployments at national level) plus the procurement overhead from in-jurisdiction siting and supply-chain export-control review.

ops_tco_opex_directional.text: factors: power / PUE, MFU-realized utilization, sovereign-clearance MLops headcount, re-certification (national + sectoral), air-gap operational overhead, downtime

provenance.source: deployment-class analyst characterization for sovereign AI operations; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with CapEx. High band (vs Fortune-500 medium) reflects the sovereign cost stack: clearance-vetted MLops headcount, multi-regime re-certification cadence, and air-gap operational discipline are structural OpEx multipliers not present in commercial enterprise deployments.

ops_lead_time.text: extended vs commercial; sovereign-program procurement gates + export-control review (BIS / national authority) typically add quarters to the order-to-power-up cycle

provenance.source: lead-time characterization for sovereign-class deployments — procurement-gate sequence (national + export-control) is the dominant variable, not vendor manufacturing capacity
provenance.notes: directional — procurement-gate + export-control sequence dominates; not a single bookable lead-time figure

ops_service_footprint.text: in-jurisdiction service / support presence required; vendor depth-of-coverage in the sovereign region is the main lever

provenance.source: service-footprint characterization for sovereign deployments — in-jurisdiction local-staff requirement narrows the OEM/ISV vendor short-list and is a structural eligibility filter
provenance.notes: directional — vendor regional presence acts as a structural eligibility filter, often before technical evaluation

ops_skills_fit.text: national talent pipeline + clearance-vetted operators; CUDA / NVAIE skills depth in the sovereign jurisdiction is the structural variable

provenance.source: skills-fit characterization for sovereign programs — national pipeline + clearance vetting are the structural constraints, not pure technical training availability
provenance.notes: directional — sovereign skills-fit is constrained by jurisdiction-resident talent + clearance pipeline; commercial CUDA/NVAIE training programs do not solve the eligibility-vetting bottleneck

segments.isv_rationale: Control (portable secure control plane for jurisdictional compliance) + capacity (national-scale datasets)
segments.battleground_note: critical battleground for the Partner-PM — flawless execution across Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Cisco, Supermicro.
segments.partner_intensity_rationale: channel-served + in-country integration/certification requirements; national procurement runs through certified OEM partners

provenance.notes: Segment definition synthesized from G42/Inception, EU AI Factory, and BIS export-control program public materials.

segments.name: Industry Verticals
segments.subtitle: Domain-specific deployments (e.g., Mayo Clinic healthcare AI)

compute_domain_accuracy.text: domain-and-dataset specific; no universal benchmark across verticals (healthcare imaging vs manufacturing visual inspection vs robotics action-prediction)

provenance.source: domain accuracy is vertical-specific and dataset-specific — Mayo Clinic clinical-decision-support benchmarks differ structurally from manufacturing defect-detection or robotics action-prediction
provenance.notes: no universal benchmark — each vertical has its own ground-truth set; do NOT present as a single cited figure

compute_safety_latency.text: vertical-defined ceiling: surgical robotics targets sub-50ms closed-loop control, medical imaging tolerates seconds in the radiologist workflow, industrial safety-stop varies by jurisdiction

provenance.source: safety-latency requirements are codified per vertical (IEC 60601 for medical devices, ISO 13482 for personal-care robotics, ISO 26262 for automotive); enforcement varies by regulator
provenance.notes: directional — vertical-defined; numerical ceilings are workload-specific, not generalizable across the industry-verticals segment

compute_edge_efficiency.text: performance-per-watt at the edge depends on deployment topology; RTX PRO 6000 and Jetson-class edge deployments operate in single-digit-to-low-double-digit TOPS/W bands for inference

provenance.source: edge-efficiency characterization for inference workloads — NVIDIA Jetson Orin family and RTX PRO product positioning materials
provenance.notes: directional — TOPS/W figures vary by precision (INT8, FP16) and workload; not a single comparable metric across vertical deployments

compute_digital_twin_sync.text: real-world → simulation update latency; bound by sensor cadence plus network latency plus simulator step time; varies by application (manufacturing line digital-twin tighter than factory-floor strategy simulation)

provenance.source: digital-twin sync characterization for manufacturing + robotics applications — NVIDIA Omniverse positioning materials, Siemens / GE / Rockwell digital-twin disclosures
provenance.notes: directional — synchronization tolerance is application-defined; numerical targets vary widely across vertical use-cases

ops_safety_certification.text: vertical-and-jurisdiction-specific certification path: FDA 510(k) or De Novo for medical devices, IEC 61508 for industrial safety, ISO 26262 for automotive ASIL levels

provenance.source: safety-certification characterization for industry verticals — FDA medical-device pathway (510(k), De Novo), IEC 61508 (functional safety), ISO 26262 (automotive)
provenance.notes: directional — certification time and cost are vertical-and-jurisdiction-specific; the ISV platform's certification track record is the dominant variable

compute_inference_p99.text: TTFT P95/P99 target ~300-500ms for interactive text-AI workloads in vertical applications (use-case dependent: chatbot ~500ms, code-completion ~100ms, batch/report tolerant to seconds). Safety-critical paths have stricter vertical-specific ceilings — see compute_safety_latency.

provenance.source: industry LLM inference SLO conventions, 2026 (Spheron, Rafay, BentoML, Mirantis) — applies to interactive text-AI in vertical deployments; safety-critical latency budgets are a separate stricter ceiling per vertical
provenance.notes: SLA convention/range — interactive text-AI only; the safety-critical latency budget is governed by compute_safety_latency and its codified vertical ceilings

ops_tco_capex_directional.text: factors: smaller cluster scale than hyperscaler/frontier; vertical-specific hardware mix (HGX plus RTX PRO 6000 edge plus Jetson plus DGX where applicable); facility readiness varies by vertical

provenance.source: deployment-class characterization for industry-vertical AI buildouts; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with OpEx. Medium band (vs Fortune-500 high / hyperscaler high) reflects smaller cluster scale and the vertical-specific hardware mix.

ops_tco_opex_directional.text: factors: domain-vetted MLops talent (rare), safety-certification cadence (recurring), vertical-specific re-validation on every model update, downtime cost in safety-critical paths

provenance.source: deployment-class characterization for industry-vertical AI operations; not a computed point value
provenance.notes: ALWAYS a directional band; never summed with CapEx. High band (despite medium CapEx) reflects that vertical-AI OpEx is dominated by certification cadence and domain-vetted talent costs — the CapEx-OpEx ratio inverts vs hyperscaler.

ops_lead_time.text: compliance-gated procurement: hardware lead-times are layered with vertical-specific certification dependencies (FDA review, ISO audit windows)

provenance.source: lead-time characterization for vertical deployments — hardware procurement is rarely the binding constraint; vertical compliance gates dominate the timeline
provenance.notes: directional — vertical compliance cycle is the dominant lead-time driver, not hardware procurement

ops_service_footprint.text: vendor depth in the vertical (NVIDIA Clara for healthcare, Omniverse for manufacturing, DRIVE for automotive, BioNeMo for life-sciences) is more important than geographic footprint

provenance.source: service-footprint characterization for vertical deployments — vendor vertical-specific product line and reference customers are the relevant lens
provenance.notes: directional — vertical-specific vendor depth matters more than geographic coverage

ops_skills_fit.text: narrow talent pool combining domain expertise (clinical, manufacturing, regulatory) with CUDA / NVAIE engineering; ISV platforms (Clara, Omniverse, BioNeMo) reduce the engineering depth required

provenance.source: skills-fit characterization for vertical deployments — talent must combine domain depth with NVIDIA-stack proficiency; ISV abstraction layers mitigate the engineering depth requirement
provenance.notes: directional — talent scarcity is structural at the domain × technical intersection; ISV platform choice is the main mitigation

architecture_blend.note: Inference-heavy edge paired with specialized training

segments.isv_rationale: Turn-key layer for limited-AI-staff orgs (hospital/factory) to deploy inference without GPU-clustering expertise
segments.partner_intensity_rationale: OEM/ISV-served (edge + regional deployments via Dell/HPE/Lenovo/Supermicro + domain ISVs), but not one of the matrix's two critical battlegrounds

provenance.notes: Segment definition synthesized from vertical AI program disclosures (healthcare, manufacturing digital twins, robotics).
